paper_title: Searching for scalar field dark matter with LIGO
coupling_convention: Lambda_gamma^-1 in GeV^-1 (paper's y-axis variable; approximate values estimated from the described frequency band and LIGO O3 sensitivity, NOT digitized from the figure)
notes: Paper (Gottel et al., arXiv:2401.18076) sets new direct-search upper limits on scalar DM couplings 1/Lambda_gamma (photon, d_e) and 1/Lambda_e (electron, d_me) from LIGO O3 data, 10 Hz to 5000 Hz (~4e-14 to ~2e-11 eV), with best improvement (up to 3 orders of magnitude over previous direct searches) in 10-180 Hz. The limit applies identically to either 1/Lambda_gamma or 1/Lambda_e assuming the other is zero; ScalarPhoton chosen per hint, but the same numbers constrain ScalarElectron (d_me = MPl/(sqrt(4pi)*Lambda_e)). No numerical table is provided in the text; the emitted data points are order-of-magnitude estimates of the Fig. 3 exclusion curve reconstructed from Eq. (10), the LIGO O3 noise curve, and integration time, hence the low extraction confidence. Assumes rho_local = 0.4 GeV/cm^3; limits at 95% C.L.
